   Kyoto University Graduate School of Management).*

2. **"Managing Expectations and Corporate Financial Policy."**
   with Ben Charoenwong and Alan Kwan. *(R&R, Review of Finance)*
   [[SSRN]](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3592103)

3. **"When Does Arbitrage Fire? Route Costs and Limits to Arbitrage."**
   Using on-chain stablecoin redemptions (Liquity's LUSD and BOLD), shows that realized
   arbitrage begins at the point implied by the measured cost of its execution route, and
   that route design shapes the direction and size of arbitrage.

4. **"Forgetting to Collect: Memory and Financial Inaction."**
   Uses 107,000 uncollected Lido staking withdrawals to separate memory from inattention in
   financial inaction, estimating a structural model of a consideration set that fades with
   time and is restored by a cue.

5. **"Private Enforcement after Public Enforcement: Evidence from the Sanction and Delisting
   of Tornado Cash."** *(Preliminary draft)*
   Uses the sanction and later delisting of Tornado Cash as a natural experiment to show that
   private screening by intermediaries, rather than the public sanction, keeps users from
   returning to a market for anonymity once enforcement is reversed.
